speed_mph: # SOURCE: EMFAC2025 v2.1.1 (California Air Resources Board), Statewide CA, Calendar Year 2026, Annual season, avg-speed bins (steady-state).
# VEHICLE MAPPING: gas_suv = EMFAC category "MDV" (Medium Duty Vehicle, ~8,501-14,000 lb GVWR; covers larger SUVs/vans/pickups), fuel=Gasoline.
#                  diesel_su_truck = EMFAC category "T6 Instate Delivery Class 6" (single-unit truck, 19,501-26,000 lb GVWR), fuel=Diesel.
#                  Smaller-SUV alternate available in raw export: "LDT2" (6,001-8,500 lb GVWR), not used here.
# CALC: fuel rate (gal/mi) = "Fuel Consumption" (1000 gal/day) x 1000 / "CVMT" (combustion VMT, mi/day), computed per speed bin from the raw export.
#       L/km = gal/mi x (3.78541 L/gal / 1.60934 km/mi) = gal/mi x 2.35215.
#       These are derived rates, not values EMFAC reports directly - spot-check against a single-vehicle EMFAC query if independent confirmation is needed.
# CAVEATS: (1) Statewide CA fleet average - reflects CARB emission standards, likely cleaner/more efficient than US national fleet average; treat as a cross-check, not a national replacement.

#          (2) T6 Instate Delivery Class 6 has no reported bin above 75 mph (heavy trucks may be governed/underrepresented at that speed in EMFAC's drive-cycle data) - 80 mph cell is blank, needs a handling decision (hold-last, extrapolate, or truncate range for this vehicle class).

#          (3) EMFAC2025 has not been EPA-approved for SIP/conformity use (per CARB's own tool disclaimer) - fine for this cost-modeling use case, flagging in case it matters for any regulatory-adjacent downstream use.
#          (4) Curves are smooth, monotonic U-shapes, minima ~40-45 mph for both classes - no non-physical artifacts observed.
